newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ left and right evenly balanced in TV1 poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ left and right evenly balanced in TV1 poll.

text.p: New Zealand's main opposition Labour Party has maintained its poll lead but the electorate is evenly split between left and right, a TV1-Colmar Brunton poll on Tuesday showed.
The poll put the centre-left Labour Party on 42 percent, up one point on the same poll a month ago.

Its ally, the five party left wing Alliance grouping, polled seven percent, unchanged, and with Labour would likely win a combined 60 seats in the 120 seat House if the poll was reflected in an election.
The next election is due in 1999.

The main government party, Prime Minister Jim Bolger's conservative National Party, was down one percentage point at 39 percent, while its junior coalition partner New Zealand First was unchanged on four percent.
The free-market Act New Zealand Party polled 4.5 percent support.

Under New Zealand's German-style Mixed Member Proportional electoral system a party must win at least five percent of the vote or at least one constituency seat to qualify for its share of the total seats.
Labour leader Helen Clark retained her lead as preferred prime minister with 24 percent support, against 20 percent for Bolger.
New Zealand First leader and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters scored four percent as preferred prime minister while Alliance leader Jim Anderton gained eight percent support.
